classification: primary architecture context; no device qualification or new grant
observations: Commands remain operational with SMMUEN clear when CMDQEN remains enabled. Disabling translation alone therefore does not explain the observed command timeout.
Consumption of a synchronization command orders completion of earlier commands in its own queue; generic command consumption has weaker semantics.
Translation-invalidation completion covers relevant translated accesses reaching their shareability domain. That scope does not identify arbitrary bypass or other-security traffic.

SMMUEN acknowledgement does not guarantee already stalled transactions have terminated. Device/interconnect-specific completion remains necessary; buffering upstream can outlive the control transition.
inference: Next raw stage/consumer samples should locate the stopping operation before changing any sequence or bound.
